(3) The middleware introduces an entirely different auth scheme (JWT via `verifyJwt`/`JWT_SECRET`) so that whenever `JWT_SECRET` is set, even `dev-token` is rejected \u2014 the contract's unconditional acceptance of `dev-token` is broken. The happy path works only in the narrow non-production/no-JWT_SECRET configuration, so the contract is largely unmet.

Main path is correct (safeParse, returns data, throws AppError with status 400, formats each issue as `path: message`), but two explicit clauses of the contract are violated. (1) The contract requires the issues be **comma-joined**; the candidate joins with `"; "` (semicolon-space), so the produced message differs from the specified format and would fail any assertion on the documented output. (2) The declared signature is `parseBody<T>(schema: ZodSchema<T>, body): T`, where `T` is the *parsed data* type; the candidate redefines `T extends z.ZodTypeAny` as the *schema* type and returns `z.infer<T>`. Inference-based call sites still work, but any caller writing the documented explicit form `parseBody<UserInput>(userSchema, body)` will fail to compile — a breaking API deviation. Additionally, the candidate silently drops the path prefix for root-level issues (emitting just `message` instead of `: message`), which is arguably nicer but is another departure from the stated `path: message` rule. Error code and throw behaviour are right, so this is not a total failure, but multiple stated clauses are unmet.
